rationale: The Parkinson study compares levodopa and subthalamic stimulation conditions in a clinical and kinematic assessment of postoperative freezing of gait. Orange appears in some supplementary plots. The measured events concern freezing and gait across medication or stimulation conditions. The original provides no raw-orange intervention or food-attributable fall-frequency estimate.

The article relates subthalamic neural signals to force-plate and motion-capture measurements of gait initiation, including freezing, in Parkinson disease. Orange identifies plotted data. No orange fruit exposure or comparative fall-frequency effect is estimated.

The report documents cardiomyopathy during clozapine treatment. An orange arrow identifies the right ventricle in an echocardiographic image. This clinical exposure is a medicine. There is no whole orange comparison or fall-frequency response in Parkinson disease.

The essential tremor study compares six adaptive eating devices and a standard spoon. Participants transferred pearl couscous to a cup near the mouth. Investigators compared transfers and device preferences. Couscous provides the same test material across devices. The experiment does not assess fresh sage, swallowing of the test food, or a Parkinson dystonia response.

The clinical imaging report examines putaminal degeneration and iron findings in multiple system atrophy. SAGE is the journal publisher. The report does not administer ground culinary sage or compare its effect on Parkinson muscle rigidity.

A case describes medically refractory seizures in an adult receiving Parkinson medication with measured vitamin B6 deficiency. The authors report resolution of seizures after pyridoxine; other clinical treatments were also involved. The reported intervention is correction of a nutrient deficiency. SAGE is the journal publisher. No ground sage exposure or sage-attributed rigidity measure was assessed.
The movement disorder report characterizes mosaic ADCY5 variants and associated clinical signs. The genetic case observations provide no dried-date comparison on pain severity in Parkinson disease.

The cardiology report considers septal ventriculoatrial timing and the diagnosis of atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia. The diagnostic timing and procedural observations give no clinical food comparison relevant to dried dates or Parkinson pain.

The pediatric report describes a child with severe vitamin C deficiency, gait difficulty, weakness and abnormal movements. The narrative reports improvement after vitamin C plus enteral nutritional supplementation. The response pertains to correction of nutritional deficiency in a child. The study neither assigns dried dates nor tests dietary pain severity in Parkinson disease.

The case report describes functional movement disorder features in one of two monozygotic twins with familial ataxia. This diagnostic comparison supplies no independently graded dried-date or Parkinson pain response.

The case reports vertical double vision after thalamic stimulation for essential tremor and explores the stimulation-related visual finding. There is no oral dried-date exposure or pain outcome in diagnosed Parkinson disease.

The case presents ileosigmoid knotting as acute abdominal obstruction, with clinical pain and surgical findings in its diagnostic history. Abdominal pain due to an acute mechanical condition supplies no dietary dried-date or Parkinson pain comparison.

The cross-sectional study assesses potentially inappropriate medicines and associated factors in nursing home residents. Medication and institutional-care variables supply no assigned dried-date exposure or food-specific pain response.

The randomized feasibility trial measures acceptability and other preliminary outcomes during home-based high-intensity interval training for people with Parkinson disease. The exposure is exercise. The paper gives no dried-date assignment or independently attributed effect on pain severity.

The comparative study assesses Parkinson disease incidence among people with type 2 diabetes receiving SGLT2 inhibitors or metformin. The population, drug exposure and disease incidence measure do not supply a dried-date intervention or pain-severity response in diagnosed Parkinson disease.

The Japanese insurance claims study evaluates prescribing patterns for Parkinson disease and compares groups by sex. Administrative dates do not identify date fruit. The article provides no dried-date or pain intervention effect.

The pure autonomic failure cohort examines biomarkers associated with later phenoconversion to central neurologic disorders, including Lewy body disease and multiple system atrophy. Diagnosis and longitudinal timing provide no dried-date exposure or Parkinson pain estimate.

The cross-sectional pilot compares hand responses to short cold-water testing in Parkinson disease and multiple system atrophy. The cold stress test is a diagnostic measurement. It supplies no dried-date exposure or comparative dietary effect on clinical Parkinson pain.

The pilot study tests repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for levodopa-induced dyskinesias in Parkinson disease and reports no clear efficacy for the tested protocol. The experimental exposure is stimulation, and the main clinical endpoint is dyskinesia. The article gives no dried-date pain comparison.

The clinical nursing study evaluates a structured touch, communication and relief program framed around spiritual care. It adds the program to standard care and measures quality of life and nursing-related outcomes. Dietary advice is part of standard care rather than a date-fruit assignment. The trial provides no independently attributed effect of dried dates on Parkinson pain.

The case describes exercise-induced cutaneous vasculitis after prolonged activity and discusses its clinical presentation. The report supplies no dried-date exposure and no attributable Parkinson pain outcome.

The comparison concerns medication responsiveness and eye-movement biomarkers. It does not measure an oral raw-fig effect on rest tremor.

The investigators document heterogeneous changes across tremor tasks. The individual diagnostic and drug-treatment narrative gives no raw-fig comparison.
